content.content: deccy new --evaluates naming any id that no sibling node document under nodes/ answers for refuses the invocation before creating anything and names each such id; nothing is created. The predicate is document presence alone — whether that document exists, not what the named node is, and not the resolution --on's ids go through — so zzzzzzzz names the root, may appear only in depends_on, and names no node document, and naming it with --evaluates names an unknown id and refuses; the root's exception is depends_on's and not this flag's.
content.rationale: Document presence is the predicate because the flag asks whether there is a node document to check, not what that node is: a richer test would make the birth read graph semantics it has no business reading, and would refuse invocations whose targets are merely odd. The root sentinel is where the paths part — zzzzzzzz owns no document, and the exception that admits it belongs to depends_on — so stating presence keeps it on the refusing side without disturbing that exception, while refusing before anything is created keeps a dangling evaluates edge out of the graph and naming each id lets the caller repair the invocation without re-deciding resolution.
